0.0.tagline: AI developer building production-grade agentic AI, RAG, and machine learning systems.
0.0.abstract: We present AA-1, an AI developer trained on four years of software and AI engineering, from robotic process automation to enterprise retrieval-augmented generation and multi-agent orchestration. AA-1 designs agent harnesses with LangGraph and LangChain, grounds LLM output with FAISS and Pinecone retrieval, and evaluates it with RAGAS and LangFuse. In production, AA-1 reduced IT issue resolution time by 84% and automated 90% of Tier-1 support. AA-1 holds a Post Graduate Diploma in Agentic AI and Machine Learning from IIT Gandhinagar and won the AI-Driven Sustainability Hackathon organised by University College London and IIT Gandhinagar.

0.7.tagline: I build agentic systems that make it to production, and I measure them once they are there.
0.7.abstract: AA-1 started out automating web content with RPA bots and now builds agent harnesses: LangGraph orchestration, sandboxed tool execution, and retrieval that keeps models grounded. At Capgemini, AA-1 shipped an enterprise RAG assistant on Vertex AI that cut IT resolution time by 84% and took over 90% of Tier-1 tickets. Along the way: a PG Diploma in Agentic AI from IIT Gandhinagar, a hackathon win with UCL, and a habit of auditing metrics before trusting them. This report covers the training run so far.

1.5.tagline: I teach LLMs to use tools, check each other's work, and occasionally behave.
1.5.abstract: AA-1 is a human, not a model, but has been fine-tuned on a lot of the same data. Pre-training: RPA bots, Java microservices, ETL pipelines. Fine-tuning: retrieval, agents, and an unreasonable number of evals. Notable emergent abilities include making support tickets disappear (84% faster, 90% automated), catching account takeovers without annoying real users, and refusing to ship a model with target leakage. Known limitations: will ask what your eval set looks like.

ablations.name: Target leakage
ablations.without: Columns that encode the label make validation scores look excellent.
ablations.with: Leaky columns audited and removed; predictions enforced by a ~600-rule fail-secure matrix.
ablations.takeaway: Audit the features before you trust the metric.

ablations.name: Grounding
ablations.without: Free-form generation answers confidently, sources or not.
ablations.with: Answer only from retrieved context, cite every claim, refuse when the answer is absent.
ablations.takeaway: Refusal is a feature. Citations make answers checkable.

ablations.name: Data split
ablations.without: A random split lets the future leak into training.
ablations.with: Time-based split, plus a naive baseline the model has to beat.
ablations.takeaway: Evaluate the way the model will be used.

ablations.name: Tool access
ablations.without: Agents read and write whatever the tools can reach.
ablations.with: Tools behind MCP with an injection guard, path-traversal checks, and a human approval gate.
ablations.takeaway: Agents get the least privilege that still does the job.

ablations.name: Raw identity data
ablations.without: The fraud model needs to hold users' personal data.
ablations.with: Privacy-first trust boundary with differential privacy and crypto-shredding.
ablations.takeaway: Security and privacy can be designed in, not bolted on.

evaluation.name: RAGAS
evaluation.what: Faithfulness, answer relevance, and context precision for RAG pipelines.

evaluation.name: LangFuse and LangSmith
evaluation.what: Traces for every agent step: inputs, tool calls, latency, and cost.

evaluation.name: CodeGraph
evaluation.what: Quality monitoring for generated code in the AI SDLC platform.

evaluation.name: Classical metrics
evaluation.what: Precision, recall, ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, and macro F1, always against a baseline.

evaluation.name: Explainability
evaluation.what: SHAP for tabular models, saliency maps for vision.

principles.title: Ground every answer
principles.text: Answers come from real documents, with sources. If the answer isn't there, the AI says so.

principles.title: Test before shipping
principles.text: Every system is checked against clear quality measures before it goes live.

principles.title: Only the access it needs
